currentAffairs.point: The GST Council held its latest meet to discuss further reforms aimed at simplifying the indirect taxation system.
currentAffairs.whyInNews: This reflects ongoing efforts by the government to improve efficiency and compliance within India’s Goods & Services Tax regime.

currentAffairs.point: Two staff members were suspended following a technical fault in an empty train at the GIFT City station.
currentAffairs.whyInNews: This highlights operational issues within India’s expanding metro infrastructure projects.

currentAffairs.point: Araku Pinery is implementing eco-tourism initiatives with new attractions like camping and seasonal farms.
currentAffairs.whyInNews: The project aims to attract tourists while promoting community involvement and sustainable practices.

currentAffairs.point: Anne Carson has been awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature for her experimental and imaginative writing.
currentAffairs.whyInNews: The award recognizes innovative approaches within literature, a field often explored during Mains exams.

currentAffairs.point: A flydubai co-pilot attempted to crash the plane into Tel Aviv airport with inspiration from the 9/11 attacks.
currentAffairs.whyInNews: This represents a direct threat to India’s strategic interests and requires immediate attention regarding aviation security protocols.

currentAffairs.point: Coal supply to power plants increased by 36% from September lows.
currentAffairs.whyInNews: This reflects a shift in demand patterns and government efforts to manage energy availability amidst potential disruptions.

currentAffairs.point: The Tea Board is increasing the number of auction centres to improve tea producer profitability.
currentAffairs.whyInNews: This reflects ongoing efforts within government to support agricultural sectors and promote fair trade practices.

currentAffairs.point: The RBI has indicated the need for central government support to combat rising inflation rates.
currentAffairs.whyInNews: This highlights the complex interplay between monetary policy and macroeconomic stability, a frequently tested topic in UPSC.

currentAffairs.point: Katie Zacharia has been appointed as the White House Press Secretary.
currentAffairs.whyInNews: Her appointment precedes key midterm congressional elections, highlighting a strategic move by the Trump administration.

currentAffairs.point: India’s greenfield investments have more than doubled China's share in 2020-25 according to the UNCTAD report.
currentAffairs.whyInNews: This reflects a growing global recognition of India as an attractive investment destination and its strategic importance within the global economy.

currentAffairs.point: The ‘Bharat Spice Map’ will align spice production with industry demand and scientific insights.
currentAffairs.whyInNews: India is a major spice exporter; this map aims to optimize its position in the global market.

currentAffairs.point: A ‘Super’ El Niño is developing, potentially leading to extreme weather events globally.
currentAffairs.whyInNews: Scientists are tracking the intensification of this event and its projected impacts on global climate patterns.

currentAffairs.point: A magnitude 7.6 earthquake struck Panama City on October 9, 2026.
currentAffairs.whyInNews: Residents are gathering outside awaiting news of the quake’s impact, indicating immediate concern and potential for damage assessment.

currentAffairs.point: The GST Council has unveiled process reforms aimed at further streamlining the administration of India’s Goods and Services Tax (GST).
currentAffairs.whyInNews: These reforms follow recent rate-related adjustments and represent a significant shift in how the tax is managed nationally.

currentAffairs.point: Weekly flight movements at Mangaluru International Airport will increase to 195 from 181 in the winter schedule.
currentAffairs.whyInNews: This reflects a shift in air travel patterns and could impact regional trade and tourism.

history.point: The Farabundo Martí National Liberation Front is founded in El Salvador.
The Outer Space Treaty comes into force.
The Partial Nuclear Test Ban Treaty comes into effect.
A United Airlines Boeing 247 is destroyed by sabotage, the first such proven case in the history of commercial aviation.
The Women's Social and Political Union is founded in support of the enfranchisement of British women.
After 20 years of construction, Vidyasagar Setu, the longest cable-stayed bridge in India, opened, joining Kolkata and Howrah.
The Partial Nuclear Test Ban Treaty, which prohibits all test detonations of nuclear weapons except for those conducted underground, went into effect.
In the first proven act of sabotage in the history of commercial aviation, a Boeing 247 operated by United Airlines exploded in mid-air near Chesterton, Indiana, killing all seven people aboard.
The Xinhai Revolution began with the Wuchang Uprising, marking the beginning of the collapse of the Qing dynasty and the establishment of the Republic of China.
In a treaty with Dutch colonial authorities, the Ndyuka people of Suriname gained territorial autonomy.

revision: The RBI has indicated the need for central government support to effectively combat rising inflation rates.
Banks and nominated agencies are now subject to IGST on gold imports at a rate of 3%.
Andhra Pradesh achieved record egg production in FY25 with 2,739 crore eggs.
India’s cumulative property tax represents only 0.15-0.2% of GDP, highlighting systemic inefficiencies in revenue collection from urban areas.
India and Ghana have signed an MoU facilitating scientific exchanges focused on crop production technology transfer.
The Union Government is holding up the approval of satellite internet services, including SpaceX's Starlink, due to security concerns.
